La voix des jeunes compte est un groupe: La voix des jeunes compte is a group of activists calling for provincial framework legislation against sexual violence in schools.
« Ce que j’aime, avec ces filles-là, c’e: “What I love about these girls is that it’s a vibe of sisterhood.” That’s how Theryanne describes her relationship with the other members of the collective she belongs to. La voix des jeunes compte is a group of activists fighting sexual violence in schools, specifically at the elementary and high school levels.
Cet organisme est formé de 23 jeunes fem: The organization is made up of 23 young women. Since 2018, they have been lobbying for provincial framework legislation against sexual violence in elementary and high schools. Today, they lead talks, workshops and various other activities, while raising awareness of the issue among young people.
Au fil de la soirée, Kenza, Sha’nyce, Th: Over the course of the evening, Kenza, Sha’nyce, Theryanne and Nerlande arrive one after another at the La Converse studios. Most of them have been involved in the collective since its founding, and they take the time to tell us about their journeys and share their realities with us.
Kenza est photographe à ses heures ; Sha: Kenza is a photographer in her spare time; Sha’nyce is a hairstylist; Theryanne is a student; and Nerlande loves creating content. “There’s so much to say about each of the girls here!” says Kenza cheerfully. The Montrealer of Moroccan origin is sure of herself: everyone present is unique. Sitting across from her, Theryanne laughs and replies, “There’s so much to say about you, too!”
Lorsqu’elle était étudiante au cégep, Ke: When she was a CEGEP student, Kenza and a few of her friends created a podcast about social justice. That’s actually how she got to know the collective, since some of its members contacted her to learn more about her involvement. “We were invited to be part of the group, along with the others from the podcast. I was really interested; I wanted to get involved in the cause.” That’s how the student joined the ranks of La voix des jeunes compte.
Entre ses cours à l’université et le dév: Between her university classes and developing her passion for photography, Kenza has a full life. She confides that for some time now, she has been questioning her identity and trying to reconnect with her Moroccan roots. “When you’re an immigrant and you grow up in a multicultural country, it can be hard to reconnect with your identity; you ask yourself a lot of questions,” she explains.
Coiffeuse à temps plein, Sha’nyce déclar: A full-time hairstylist, Sha’nyce says school wasn’t really made for her. “After a year of post-secondary studies in special education, I decided to stop and dedicate myself completely to hairstyling. I was already doing it on the side while in school; it’s been my passion for a long time,” she explains. She tells us she finds it ironic, because she didn’t like hairstyling at first. “My mother is also a hairstylist. At first, I hated it. I never would have imagined working in this field,” she says.
Aujourd’hui, Sha’nyce prend beaucoup la: Today, Sha’nyce does a lot of the speaking for the collective. Deeply involved, she explains that it’s because she “takes this cause to heart, a cause that, in her view, should raise awareness among everyone from the youngest age.”
À sa deuxième année en sciences humaines: In her second year of social sciences at CEGEP, Theryanne has a strong interest in criminology and helping relationships. That’s one of the things that pushed her to get involved with the collective. “I’ve been here since well before the group was created, well over five years,” she points out. “I think what speaks to me most, beyond my passion for the cause, is the feeling of female solidarity between us.”
D’origine haïtienne et dominicaine, Ther: Of Haitian and Dominican origin, Theryanne is happy to have found herself in a healthy sisterhood by getting involved in the group. “It lets us heal from some of the hurts we can go through growing up, in a way,” she adds.
Également impliquée depuis la création d: Also involved since the project began, Nerlande is passionate about content creation. “I have a YouTube channel where I post vlogs,” she tells us, half shy, half cheerful. Taking part in awareness activities allows her to push past her limits. “My goal here is to get out of my comfort zone and get involved in important social change,” she says.
De nature réservée, Nerlande explique co: Reserved by nature, Nerlande explains how the collective has helped her assert herself. “By speaking in public and taking care of social media, I was able to open up and communicate more easily with the outside world, something I’ve often struggled with,” she explains.
« À la base, avant qu’on ne se retrouve: “Originally, before we came together around the same cause, most of us already knew each other well. We all lived in the same neighbourhood,” Theryanne recalls with a smile. “The proximity of our schools and of the places we hung out when we were younger created a kind of longstanding bond between us.” What has strengthened the existing bond between these four agents of change is the solidarity and the hardships they’ve faced while defending their cause over the past several years.

En 2017, une loi a été adoptée pour prév: In 2017, a law was passed to prevent this violence in CEGEPs and universities, but no provision exists for elementary and high schools. It is because of this lack of prevention in schools that the collective was born. Wanting to respond to young people’s demands, the group is calling for a law to be passed to that end.
« On a toutes été au secondaire. Voir qu: “We all went to high school. To see that none of us was protected from that is very serious,” says Kenza. By “that,” the young woman is referring to sexual violence, which is present in elementary and high schools.
« On a fait énormément de représentation: “We’ve made a huge number of representations to politicians to address this need,” Kenza continues. “But we’re starting to get fed up. We’ve said everything there was to say!” Theryanne retorts. “That doesn’t mean we’re going to stop. We’re just finding other ways to get involved in support of this cause.”
S’impliquer autrement, c’est l’une des p: Getting involved differently is one of the phrases at the heart of their actions. Sha’nyce has made it her rallying cry. She spends a lot of time in schools, in the field with young people, and acknowledges that you have to act realistically: “Nobody’s 13 and dedicated to attending conferences. The reality is that you have to reach young people in their everyday environment,” she explains.
Les filles font un travail positif et in: The girls do positive, inspiring work that is both serious and institutional (they organize press conferences, for example) and also inspiring and personal (they hold awareness workshops with students). But they also go through less rosy episodes. Kenza brings this up: “When we speak in public or take part in political events to make representations, we always have to be careful about what we say and be politically correct. Why? Well, we’re a collective made up of Black and Arab women.”
« De manière générale, en tant que femme: “In general, as a woman, you already have to be careful; but it’s even more true when you’re part of a minority. You can’t be too angry, you can’t be too emotional, you can’t cry, and the list goes on! You have to be very careful, otherwise all the work you do will be ignored and everything will be turned against you,” Kenza lists.
Malgré ces doubles – parfois triples – s: Despite these double – sometimes triple – standards and the intersectionality (the multiplication of oppressions) that the four young women experience, they keep their heads high. “I think we’re very strong. I don’t know who else could endure as much as we do,” Kenza says.
D’autres expériences, plus personnelles,: Other, more personal experiences have tested the girls in the past. Sha’nyce, for instance, once found herself in a situation where, intending to report an unhealthy situation involving sexual violence, she saw her intervention turned against her. “They made me feel bad. They put the blame on me, and I got hurt while I was helping someone close to me in a dangerous situation,” she recalls sadly.
« Aujourd’hui, je réalise que c’est un p: “Today, I realize it was a small harm for a greater good. I don’t regret reporting what I saw because, in the end, I kind of saved the victim, who didn’t realize how serious the situation was,” she explains without going into detail. “I can’t carry the burden of everyone who could be a victim, but just having been able to help one person, I consider that I’ve accomplished something big,” she continues.
« Il ne faut pas non plus négliger le fa: “We also can’t overlook the fact that some of us have been campaigning for the same thing for more than five years but haven’t seen any results from the authorities. From talking and repeating ourselves so much, we wear ourselves out,” adds Kenza.
Kenza, Sha’nyce, Theryanne et Nerlande r: Kenza, Sha’nyce, Theryanne and Nerlande constantly come back to the strength of the bond that unites them, especially when it comes to facing difficulties. “When one of us cries, no matter the reason, the others are always there to reassure her. We’re a shoulder for each other, we’re always there for one another!” exclaims Sha’nyce. And that “vibe of sisterhood,” an expression the four friends repeat several times, is what makes the collective unique.
Theryanne souligne d’ailleurs combien il: Theryanne also stresses how important it is to stick together when working on a subject like sexual violence. “Like it or not, sexual violence is a subject you have to handle with kid gloves,” she says. “It’s extremely sensitive. You need a certain thick skin, even resilience, to talk about it.”
« Ce qu’on fait, c’est avant tout pour l: “What we do is first and foremost for young people,” says Sha’nyce, taking the floor. “La voix des jeunes compte is, above all, young people’s voice!”
Elle est immédiatement suivie de Nerland: Nerlande immediately follows, with a special message she wants to address to young people: “Perseverance is the most important thing. Most of the time, people won’t see all the work you’re doing, but the most important thing is not to stop. Everything bears fruit,” she says solemnly. She also asks young people to always keep believing in their projects and in their future, because they “are themselves the future they want to see.”
« Une partie de moi, c’est ce collectif: “A part of me is this collective; I live my life through it,” Sha’nyce resumes. “Go for it! If you have an idea in your head, do it. If you think there are plenty of obstacles, persevere and I’m convinced you’ll get where you want to be,” she says with such conviction that you’d think there was a young person sitting right in front of her.
